parameter_default_encoding: In this registry only, JSON null in a parameter default field means no declared default and is not the LCL NULL value. A non-null default is the exact declared value applied only when an optional parameter is MISSING; required parameters never acquire a default.

contract_type_notation.purpose: The closed machine-readable notation in which every operation-contract and result-schema type string in this release is written. It fixes one exact reading for each such string so that two conforming implementations resolve the same contract type from the same registry bytes.
contract_type_notation.separation_from_source_syntax: This registry notation does not extend LCL source syntax. A spelling is admissible in a source TYPE field only when the independent TYPE_EXPRESSION grammar in 04_GRAMMAR/10_COMPLETE_EBNF.ebnf and the field-signature value kind admit it. Shared built-in names denote the same types in both notations; registry-only unions, metatypes, and schema names do not become source forms.

grammar.notation_profile: ISO 14977 profile identical to 04_GRAMMAR/10_COMPLETE_EBNF.ebnf: comma concatenates, vertical bar alternates, braces repeat zero or more times, square brackets enclose an optional part, and question marks delimit a special sequence.
productions: MEMBER = ENUM_FORM | COLLECTION_FORM | REFERENCE_FORM | QUALIFIED_IDENTIFIER_FORM | ATOM ;
ATOM = SCALAR_TYPE_NAME | SPECIAL_VALUE_NAME | META_TYPE_NAME | NAMED_VALUE_KIND | RESULT_RECORD_NAME | TYPE_VARIABLE ;

SCALAR_TYPE_NAME.meaning: One built-in scalar type name. The parameterized rows LIST[T], SET[T], and REFERENCE[T] name constructors and are not scalar atoms.

SPECIAL_VALUE_NAME.meaning: One special value name. NULL also resolves as a scalar type name; MISSING and UNKNOWN resolve only here.

BLOCK_NAME.meaning: One declared block name, used only as a reference target.

NAMED_VALUE_KIND.meaning: One named value kind, cited by its exact registered lowercase key. Citing the definition does not admit source field syntax into this notation.

RESULT_RECORD_NAME.meaning: One closed result-side record schema name.

DOMAIN_NAME.meaning: One declared qualified-identifier domain, resolved by that registry's own source, pointer, and selection record.

ENUM_VALUE.meaning: One member of the exhaustive value set written inside its own ENUM form. The set is closed by that form and resolves against no external registry.

lexical_rules: No whitespace character may occur anywhere in a contract type string.
An atom written only in ASCII uppercase letters, digits, and underscore is a language-level name: a scalar type name, a special value name, or a block name.
An atom containing any ASCII lowercase letter is a specification-level designator: a meta-type name, a named value kind, or a result record name.
One ASCII uppercase letter standing alone is a type variable, never a scalar type name; every registered scalar type name is at least four characters long.

A constructor keyword is consumed structurally before atom resolution, so it is never classified as an atom even where the same word is separately registered as a type name or value kind, as ENUM and qualified_identifier are. ENUM, LIST, and SET are valid only with their bracketed argument, and a bare occurrence is invalid.
Comparison of every atom against its declared source is exact and case-sensitive.
union_rules: A union denotes the set of its members; member order carries no meaning, and two strings whose member sets are equal at every position denote the same contract type.
A member may not repeat within one union, one reference domain, or one enum value set.
Every union, reference domain, and enum value set has at least one member; an empty alternative is invalid.
A union inside a collection argument, a reference domain, or an enum value set binds no tighter or looser than the brackets that enclose it, so no precedence rule is required.

nesting.depth_definition: The number of bracketed constructor forms enclosing a member, counting the outermost bracketed form as depth 1.
nesting.rule: A contract type string whose nesting exceeds maximum_depth is invalid.

omitted_parameter.REFERENCE: REFERENCE without a bracketed domain admits any reference target.
omitted_parameter.qualified_identifier: qualified_identifier without a parenthesized domain admits any registered qualified identifier.

type_variable_binding.scope: One operation invocation, spanning the invoked operation's own contract and the result schema that contract selects.
type_variable_binding.rule: Every occurrence of one type variable within that scope denotes the same type, fixed by the resolved target or argument that first binds it. A type variable carries no meaning across different operation contracts and is never resolved from a registry.
type_variable_binding.worked_example: core.filter declares target LIST[T] and selects result.collection, whose items field is LIST[T]; both denote the same member type for one invocation.

invalid_forms: A leading, trailing, or doubled vertical bar.
An empty bracket or parenthesis pair.
A repeated member within one union, reference domain, or enum value set.
An atom that resolves against no declared source.
A qualified_identifier domain that no declared domain record names.
ENUM without a bracketed value set, or LIST or SET without a bracketed argument.
A reference domain member that is neither a block name, a meta-type name, nor a scalar type name.
An uppercase spelling of a named value kind, a meta-type name, or a result record name.
A lowercase spelling of a scalar type name, a special value name, or a block name.
contract_type_notation.defect_rule: A contract type string that does not parse under this notation, or whose atom does not resolve against its declared source, is a defect in this specification and is repaired in the registry. It is never a document diagnostic, never selects a registered error, and never reaches a conforming document.

axis_contract.custom_operation_resolution: A custom kind.operation declares its complete axis contract in its own DEFINE block and selects no implementation profile. SIDE_EFFECT FALSE declares possible_effects exactly none. A SIDE_EFFECT effect-class LIST declares one or more distinct concrete effect classes, excludes none, and is that operation's possible_effects maximum. DEPENDENCY declares the possible_dependencies maximum from the closed dependency vocabulary; an omitted DEPENDENCY declares exactly declared_state_only. Resolve the invocation effect set from the address classes of the resolved target and declared destination arguments under the same address-class rules that bind core rows, bounded by the declared maximum; an invocation that resolves an effect class outside that maximum, and an effect-class declaration whose invocation resolves no concrete effect class, each emit error.operation.precondition before effects. DETERMINISTIC TRUE requires the declared contract to satisfy determinism_identity over identical declared inputs and declared dependency snapshots; DETERMINISTIC FALSE conservatively permits either final category and never relaxes another rule. The declaration supplies the final category and the dependency and effect sets used by an ACTION graph.
axis_contract.determinism_identity: For a deterministic operation, identical declared inputs, dependency snapshots, selected profile-role bindings, and implementation versions require semantically equivalent results, effects, ordering, and status.
axis_contract.dependency_resolution: possible_dependencies is the registry maximum. Resolve the invocation dependency set from the target, source, destination, selected profile, arguments, and referenced execution graph. When no external capability is selected, the invocation set is exactly declared_state_only.
axis_contract.effect_resolution: possible_effects is the registry maximum. Resolve the invocation effect set from the selected targets, destinations, profiles, arguments, and referenced execution graph. When no observable effect can occur, the invocation set is exactly none.

category_definitions.read_only: Observes or computes without authorizing any observable effect; possible_effects is exactly none.
category_definitions.mutating: May change an external or addressable target; the permitted effect classes remain exactly bounded by possible_effects.
category_definitions.memory_state: Writes an LCL MEMORY or STATE target; the permitted effect classes remain exactly bounded by possible_effects.
category_definitions.control: Coordinates, delegates, stops, resumes, retries, or cancels execution, or requests authoritative input; the permitted effect classes remain exactly bounded by possible_effects.

dependency_definitions.declared_state_only: Reads only declared LCL values, immutable definitions, and invocation-local or internal execution snapshots; selects no host, network, model, or human capability.
dependency_definitions.host: Reads or invokes an addressable resource or capability supplied by the execution host, excluding any separately declared network, model, or human capability.
dependency_definitions.network: Reads from or invokes a remote endpoint or transport capability; this dependency alone is not a network effect.
dependency_definitions.model: Obtains inference or generation from the selected LC or model capability.
dependency_definitions.human: Obtains an authoritative response or decision from a human.

effect_definitions.none: Produces no observable state change or outbound communication and is exclusive.
effect_definitions.filesystem: Creates, changes, moves, or deletes filesystem content or metadata.
effect_definitions.network: Performs a primary transfer, copy, download, upload, or publication over a network, or creates, changes, or removes network-addressed content. Remote access used only as observation or computation input is a dependency. Remote transport used only to realize a process, package, message, memory, or state effect is not an additional network effect.
effect_definitions.process: Starts, executes, stops, or otherwise changes a native process or service.
effect_definitions.package: Changes installed package state or package-manager records.
effect_definitions.message: Sends an externally observable message or request to a recipient.
effect_definitions.state: Changes an LCL STATE or OUTPUT target, an authorized addressable target not classified as filesystem, network, or memory, or internal execution-unit or lifecycle state.

marker_definitions.inherited: Resolve the marked axis exactly and transitively from the referenced ACTION; this marker appears only on core.retry and never combines with another member.

implementation_profile.selection: When an operation contract names one or more selected or implementation profile roles, the exact operation identifier, profile role, target or address class, arguments, implementation identifier, and implementation version select exactly one immutable profile for each role before effects.
implementation_profile.role_resolution: all applies to every invocation of that core operation. For core.execute, non_graph applies exactly to PATH, URI, or STRING targets and graph applies exactly to REFERENCE[TASK|PHASE|SEQUENCE|ACTION|TEST] targets; graph mode has no local execution profile and resolves every reachable operation profile transitively. A core operation absent from required_roles_by_operation requires no local core profile. A custom kind.operation selects no profile role and resolves under axis_contract.custom_operation_resolution. No unlisted local profile role may be selected.
implementation_profile.determinism_category_domain: A profile declares exactly one final category: deterministic or nondeterministic. derived and inherited are operation-row resolution markers and are forbidden as profile categories.
implementation_profile.bounds: For bounds checking, declared_state_only denotes an empty set of external dependency classes and none denotes an empty set of concrete effect classes. A core profile may narrow but never widen the row's concrete dependency or effect maxima; an empty narrowed set is represented exactly by its sentinel. A profile selected by a deterministic base row must declare deterministic; a nondeterministic profile is out of bounds. A custom kind.operation declares its own maxima from the same closed vocabularies in its DEFINE block. Every profile's invocation rule resolves actual sets within its maxima.
implementation_profile.determinism_resolution: A deterministic base row remains deterministic and accepts only a deterministic profile. A nondeterministic base row resolves deterministic only when its immutable profile removes every permitted variation and declares an exact source satisfying determinism_identity; otherwise it remains nondeterministic. A derived row applies the exact operation-specific mapping named by its derivation source to the final categories of every resolved profile and/or graph. DETERMINISTIC TRUE is verified afterward and never causes category narrowing.
implementation_profile.graph_resolution: For TASK, PHASE, SEQUENCE, ACTION, or TEST references, emit error.reference.cycle and fail before axis resolution when a prohibited reference cycle exists, then resolve every reachable core row profile or custom kind.operation declaration to a final category and invocation sets. The graph is deterministic exactly when every reachable resolved operation is deterministic, including when no operation is reachable; it is nondeterministic when any reachable resolved operation is nondeterministic. Form each transitive union from concrete external dependency classes and concrete effect classes only: omit declared_state_only when any external dependency is present and otherwise return exactly declared_state_only; omit none when any concrete effect is present and otherwise return exactly none.
implementation_profile.failure: A missing, ambiguous, incomplete, or out-of-bounds required profile role emits error.operation.precondition and fails before effects.

core.inspect.meaning: Observe metadata or structure without changing the target.

determinism.source: Exact metadata projection from the resolved target snapshot under the selected implementation version.

core.inspect.invocation_resolution: Resolve host for PATH, host-bound, or host-backed REFERENCE access and host plus network for URI access; otherwise resolve declared_state_only. A depth outside 0..100 produces error.value.out_of_range. The invocation has no effects.
preconditions: target exists
postconditions: target bytes/state unchanged

core.read.meaning: Retrieve accessible exact content without changing its source.

determinism.source: Exact requested content, range, and format from the resolved target snapshot.

core.read.invocation_resolution: Resolve dependencies from the target address class and requested range or format; URI access adds network. The invocation has no effects.

range.meaning: Closed zero-based half-open selection in the target representation.
constraints: When supplied, range is an OBJECT with exactly unit: STRING, start: INTEGER, and end: INTEGER. No other keys or defaults are admitted. unit is exactly scalar, line, item, or byte.

Resolve the exact target representation and any requested format before selecting the range. scalar requires STRING and indexes Unicode scalars; line requires STRING and indexes LF-terminated lines, retaining each selected line terminator and any final unterminated line. Empty STRING has zero lines. item requires LIST[T] and indexes elements. byte requires LIST[INTEGER] with every element in 0..255; BYTES is not content.

Require 0 <= start <= end <= sequence length; otherwise error.value.out_of_range. Return the same representation family containing exactly positions start through end-1; equal bounds produce the corresponding empty value. No clipping or ambient encoding conversion occurs. An incompatible unit/representation or wrong key/type uses error.operation.parameter.

preconditions: target exists and is readable
postconditions: target bytes/state unchanged
result is the exact requested representation, or its range selection under the closed range contract

core.analyze.meaning: Derive stated findings from declared input.

determinism.source: The base model or analytical method may vary only within the declared criteria and method constraints.

core.analyze.invocation_resolution: Resolve exactly one immutable analysis profile for every invocation, then resolve model from the selected analytical method and host or network from an addressable target. A non-generative deterministic analysis profile may narrow the nondeterministic base only under axis_contract.implementation_profile; any kind.operation DETERMINISTIC TRUE is checked afterward against the resolved final category.
preconditions: all evidence sources are declared
postconditions: findings distinguish observed facts from inference

core.calculate.meaning: Compute a result from declared values and rules.

determinism.source: The registered expression, binding, numeric, division, and rounding rules fix the result.

core.calculate.invocation_resolution: Use only the declared target value, expression, bindings, and declared snapshots. Evaluate MISSING and UNKNOWN under operators_and_functions_v0.1.0.json#/evaluation_contract, including ==, !=, and EXISTS exceptions; a required final MISSING result produces error.required.missing and UNKNOWN produces error.value.unknown. A host-capacity failure is error.host.constraint and does not change the dependency class. Parse and bind the exact expression_fragment_contract; no alternate calculation language is admitted.

expression.meaning: One expression fragment STRING, or REF to a DEFINE kind.constant whose declared value is such a STRING.
constraints: Follow expression_fragment_contract; a REFERENCE must resolve exactly once to DEFINE kind.constant with TYPE STRING.
Follow expression_fragment_contract bindings; no reserved or declaration-name shadowing.

preconditions: expression and bindings type-check
postconditions: result equals exact expression semantics
core.calculate.error_resolution: Union local errors with every applicable diagnostic of the decoded expression; wrong reference declaration kind uses error.reference.kind.

core.compare.meaning: Compare artifacts or values against exact criteria.

determinism.source: The resolved operand snapshots and exact comparison criteria fix the result.

core.compare.invocation_resolution: Resolve host or network independently for the target and against operands; material-value-only comparison resolves declared_state_only. When criteria is omitted, use the registered == exact strict-equality comparison over the resolved operands. Evaluate the single criterion under the registered operator and sentinel rules: a non-==/!= criterion encountering MISSING produces error.required.missing, and a criterion whose result remains UNKNOWN produces error.value.unknown because a successful result.value must contain a material value. The invocation has no effects.

criteria.meaning: Exact comparison criteria; omission selects the registered == strict-equality comparison.
constraints: One STRING is exactly one of ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, IN, CONTAINS, MATCHES.

One OBJECT is closed with required operator (one permitted STRING token), optional left (property_path STRING), and optional right (property_path STRING). Omitted paths select the complete corresponding operand; supplied paths project through exact registered OBJECT fields.
One REFERENCE resolves once to a declared STRING or OBJECT value satisfying the same contract; it never invokes an operation.

Unknown keys, malformed paths, absent operator, and an unregistered token produce error.operation.parameter. A missing projected value is MISSING and follows the selected operator sentinel rules; an incompatible operand pair produces error.operator.operand.

preconditions: both operands are accessible and criteria are type-valid
postconditions: Exactly one comparison is evaluated and result.value.value is its BOOLEAN result; FALSE is a successful comparison result, not an operation failure.

determinism.source: No mandatory strategy pins returned cardinality, complete subset, or order even when every returned member satisfies the predicate.

core.select.invocation_resolution: Evaluate a type-compatible predicate from declared values and snapshots. A predicate result of MISSING produces error.required.missing and UNKNOWN produces error.value.unknown. A referenced kind.operation must resolve to deterministic, side-effect-free behavior with dependencies exactly declared_state_only; no invocation may add a dependency or effect.

constraints: A REFERENCE resolves exactly once to a kind.operation with SIDE_EFFECT FALSE, DETERMINISTIC TRUE, a fully resolved dependency set of exactly declared_state_only, exactly one PARAMETER accepting the member type, and exactly one BOOLEAN RESULT.
A STRING follows expression_fragment_contract with the reserved item binding and must produce BOOLEAN; final MISSING and UNKNOWN retain their registered errors.

preconditions: predicate accepts the member type
postconditions: every returned member is one target member occurrence for which predicate is TRUE
no target member occurrence is returned more than once
result cardinality is any integer from zero through the number of TRUE target member occurrences
the selected TRUE subset and result order are otherwise unspecified
core.select.error_resolution: Union the local errors with every applicable error of the referenced predicate operation when a predicate REFERENCE is selected. A STRING predicate retains all applicable expression diagnostics.

core.filter.meaning: Return all members of one LIST that satisfy a predicate, preserving source order.

determinism.source: All and only TRUE members are returned in their exact LIST source order.

core.filter.invocation_resolution: Resolve the predicate to a deterministic side-effect-free expression over declared values or a kind.operation whose fully resolved dependency set is exactly declared_state_only. A predicate result of MISSING produces error.required.missing and UNKNOWN produces error.value.unknown. No invocation may add a dependency or effect.

constraints: A REFERENCE resolves exactly once to a kind.operation with SIDE_EFFECT FALSE, DETERMINISTIC TRUE, a fully resolved dependency set of exactly declared_state_only, exactly one PARAMETER accepting the member type, and exactly one BOOLEAN RESULT.
A STRING follows expression_fragment_contract with the reserved item binding and must produce BOOLEAN; final MISSING and UNKNOWN retain their registered errors.

preconditions: target is LIST[T] and predicate accepts T
postconditions: source order is preserved
all and only TRUE members are returned
core.filter.error_resolution: Union the local errors with every applicable error of the referenced predicate operation when a predicate REFERENCE is selected. A STRING predicate retains all applicable expression diagnostics.

core.sort.meaning: Return LIST[T] in one declared deterministic total order from LIST[T] or SET[T].

determinism.source: Derived from operators_and_functions_v0.1.0.json#/ordered_types, #/ordered_type_rules, the registered property-access projection or validated key operation, original LIST source position for ties, and the distinct-key rule for SET members: every valid invocation resolves deterministic; an invocation that cannot satisfy those rules fails.

core.sort.invocation_resolution: Resolve natural order, one property_path, or one validated deterministic side-effect-free key operation whose fully resolved dependency set is exactly declared_state_only. No invocation may add a dependency or effect.

key.meaning: Optional total-order projection; STRING is one exact property_path and REFERENCE is one validated kind.operation extractor.
constraints: Omission is legal only when every pair of target members is mutually order-compatible under operators_and_functions_v0.1.0.json#/ordered_types.
A STRING is exactly one property_path defined for every target member.

A REFERENCE resolves to a kind.operation with SIDE_EFFECT FALSE, DETERMINISTIC TRUE, a fully resolved dependency set of exactly declared_state_only, exactly one PARAMETER accepting T, and exactly one RESULT of a concrete registered ordered type.
Every key value is present, known, and mutually order-compatible; distinct SET members produce distinct keys.
descending reverses primary-key order without reversing original LIST source order among equal-key members

preconditions: an omitted key requires mutually order-compatible target members
a declared key is defined for every member and produces present, known, mutually order-compatible values
distinct SET members produce distinct keys
postconditions: result.collection.items is LIST[T]
the result contains exactly the target members, preserving LIST multiplicity and including each SET member once
ordering follows the natural value or declared key and direction
equal-key LIST members retain original LIST source order

diagnostic_triggers.error.operation.parameter: A missing required TARGET, or an unknown, duplicate, or positional parameter, including unregistered stable or comparator.
diagnostic_triggers.error.reference.unresolved: The key REFERENCE does not resolve exactly once.
diagnostic_triggers.error.reference.kind: The key REFERENCE resolves to a declaration other than kind.operation.
diagnostic_triggers.error.required.missing: A declared key value is MISSING for any member.
diagnostic_triggers.error.value.unknown: A declared key value is UNKNOWN for any member.
diagnostic_triggers.error.operation.precondition: An omitted key lacks natural total order; a STRING key is not one well-formed property_path defined for every member; a key-operation signature is incompatible; key values are not mutually order-compatible; distinct SET members produce equal keys; or the key operation has invalid determinism, effects, dependencies, or a missing, ambiguous, incomplete, or out-of-bounds immutable profile.

core.sort.error_resolution: Union the local errors with every applicable error of the referenced key operation when a key REFERENCE is selected.

core.group.meaning: Partition one LIST by one declared key, preserving deterministic group and member order.

determinism.source: The exact deterministic key partitions every LIST member into exactly one group; groups follow first key occurrence and members retain source order.

core.group.invocation_resolution: Resolve STRING key as exactly one property_path under field_signatures_v0.1.0.json, or REFERENCE as the registered deterministic side-effect-free key operation with dependencies exactly declared_state_only. A key result of MISSING produces error.required.missing and UNKNOWN produces error.value.unknown. No invocation may add a dependency or effect.

constraints: A REFERENCE resolves exactly once to a kind.operation with SIDE_EFFECT FALSE, DETERMINISTIC TRUE, a fully resolved dependency set of exactly declared_state_only, exactly one PARAMETER accepting the member type, and exactly one material RESULT usable as a grouping key.
A STRING is exactly one property_path defined for every member; malformed or statically unregistered paths produce error.operation.precondition.

preconditions: target is LIST[T] and key is defined for every T member
postconditions: result.value.value is a LIST of closed OBJECT records containing exactly key and items; key is the evaluated material grouping key and items is LIST[T].
Group keys are compared by the registered strict == equality, with no coercion; every input member occurrence appears in exactly one items LIST.
Groups follow first key occurrence and members within each group retain LIST source order; an empty input yields an empty LIST with the same group-record schema.
core.group.error_resolution: Union the local errors with every applicable error of the referenced key operation when a key REFERENCE is selected.

core.validate.meaning: Check syntax, type, reference, dependency, and constraints before effects.

determinism.source: The closed syntax, type, reference, dependency, schema, and constraint rules fix the validation result.

core.validate.invocation_resolution: Resolve host or network only for addressable targets or referenced schemas and rules; material-value-only validation resolves declared_state_only. The invocation has no effects.

constraints: The REFERENCE resolves exactly once, following transparent aliases, to a kind.type whose resolved type is OBJECT and whose schema applies to the target. Material OBJECT schema encodings are not admitted.
Every REFERENCE resolves exactly once to a VALIDATE declaration applicable to the target.

preconditions: validation has no external side effect
postconditions: all detected failures use registered error identifiers

determinism.source: Derived from deterministic evaluation of the resolved assertion against the observed target snapshot and the immutable verification profile: the invocation copies that profile's final category.

core.verify.invocation_resolution: Resolve the assertion as a side-effect-free BOOLEAN_EXPRESSION or a REFERENCE to one declared BOOLEAN value or expression snapshot; it never invokes an operation or profile. Resolve observation dependencies and exactly one immutable verification profile from the target and evidence sources; URI observation adds network. Verification itself has no effects.

constraints: A REFERENCE resolves exactly once to a declared BOOLEAN value or expression snapshot and never invokes an operation or profile.

preconditions: target is observable
postconditions: result records TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN and evidence

core.test.meaning: Evaluate one declared comparison, optionally after executing one referenced TASK or ACTION.

determinism.source: Derived from the supplied assertion or expected-and-actual comparison and, when TARGET is a TASK or ACTION, its resolved reachable execution graph: comparison-only mode is deterministic; reference-execution mode copies the graph's final category before deterministic comparison.

core.test.invocation_resolution: Exactly one comparison form is always supplied: assertion, or expected with exactly one actual source. Expected-and-actual form always uses the registered == strict-equality operator. A material-value TARGET is the actual source; without a TASK or ACTION TARGET, comparison resolves dependencies to declared_state_only and effects to none. With a TASK or ACTION TARGET, execute its reachable graph, resolve its final determinism category and normalized transitive dependency and effect unions under axis_contract.implementation_profile.graph_resolution, then evaluate the supplied assertion or registered == comparison.

constraints: A REFERENCE resolves exactly once to a declared BOOLEAN value or expression snapshot and never invokes an operation or profile.
A REFERENCE resolves exactly once to a declared material-value snapshot after any referenced TASK or ACTION completes and never invokes another operation or profile.

preconditions: exactly one comparison form is supplied: assertion; or expected together with exactly one actual source, either the actual parameter or a material-value TARGET
a material-value TARGET is legal only as the actual source for expected, cannot accompany actual, and cannot accompany assertion
a TASK or ACTION TARGET is executed before the supplied comparison and TARGET alone is not a complete test
postconditions: passed reflects the supplied assertion or registered == strict-equality comparison after any referenced execution completes
core.test.error_resolution: Union the local errors, including error.reference.cycle for a prohibited graph cycle, with every applicable error of the referenced TASK or ACTION graph when reference-execution mode is selected.

core.report.meaning: Produce a factual report from declared results and evidence.

determinism.source: Base model-authored wording may vary while facts, inferences, missing values, unknown values, format, and evidence constraints remain invariant.

core.report.invocation_resolution: Resolve exactly one immutable reporting profile for every invocation and the selected reporting method. A structured or rule-based deterministic reporting profile may narrow the nondeterministic base only under axis_contract.implementation_profile; any kind.operation DETERMINISTIC TRUE is checked afterward against the resolved final category. Reporting itself has no effects.
preconditions: all report sources are declared
postconditions: report distinguishes facts, inference, missing, and unknown

core.return.meaning: Return one declared value to the invoking channel.

determinism.source: The returned value equals the exactly resolved target value.

core.return.invocation_resolution: Resolve only the declared material value or REFERENCE. A REFERENCE that does not resolve exactly once produces error.reference.unresolved; one that resolves to MISSING produces error.required.missing, and one that resolves to UNKNOWN produces error.value.unknown. Returning a material value adds no effects.
preconditions: target resolves to a material value other than MISSING or UNKNOWN
postconditions: returned value equals resolved target value

core.create.meaning: Establish an authorized target with the declared content or type.

determinism.source: The target pre-state, content or target type, fail-if-exists flag, and selected target profile fix the required post-state.

core.create.invocation_resolution: Classify a REFERENCE target by the address class of its resolved target, never by REFERENCE syntax. PATH mutation adds host dependency and filesystem effect; URI mutation adds network dependency and network effect; OUTPUT or another authorized non-filesystem, non-network, non-memory, non-STATE addressable target adds state effect and its required dependency. MEMORY and STATE targets are prohibited; use core.memory_write or core.state_update.

fail_if_exists.meaning: Reject an existing target when TRUE; when FALSE, permit replacing or reconciling it to the declared post-state.

preconditions: target is not MEMORY or STATE; those mutations use core.memory_write or core.state_update
target does not exist when fail_if_exists is TRUE
at least content or target_type is supplied
postconditions: target exists
content/type matches parameters

core.write.meaning: Establish or replace complete content of an authorized target.

determinism.source: The exact replacement content, create-if-missing flag, target snapshot, and selected write profile fix the required post-state.

core.write.invocation_resolution: Classify a REFERENCE target by the address class of its resolved target, never by REFERENCE syntax. PATH mutation adds host dependency and filesystem effect; URI mutation adds network dependency and network effect; OUTPUT or another authorized non-filesystem, non-network, non-memory, non-STATE addressable target adds state effect and its required dependency. MEMORY and STATE targets are prohibited; use core.memory_write or core.state_update.
preconditions: target is not MEMORY or STATE; those mutations use core.memory_write or core.state_update
target exists unless create_if_missing is TRUE
postconditions: complete target content equals content parameter

core.append.meaning: Add content at the declared end of an authorized target.

determinism.source: The target pre-state remains the exact prefix and the declared content is the exact suffix.

core.append.invocation_resolution: Classify a REFERENCE target by the address class of its resolved target, never by REFERENCE syntax. PATH mutation adds host dependency and filesystem effect; URI mutation adds network dependency and network effect; OUTPUT or another authorized non-filesystem, non-network, non-memory, non-STATE addressable target adds state effect and its required dependency. MEMORY and STATE targets are prohibited; use core.memory_write or core.state_update.

constraints: Content and the selected mutable destination value have the same family: STRING appends exact Unicode scalars; LIST[T] appends elements of the identical element type T. No serialization or implicit conversion occurs; BYTES is a count and is not content.

preconditions: target is not MEMORY or STATE; those mutations use core.memory_write or core.state_update
target exists and supports append
postconditions: content is the exact suffix appended to the destination value under same-family concatenation; existing prefix and source content remain unchanged

core.modify.meaning: Change selected content or properties of an existing target.

determinism.source: The exact change, bounded selection, optional pre-state guard, target snapshot, and selected change profile fix the permitted post-state.

core.modify.invocation_resolution: Classify a REFERENCE target by the address class of its resolved target, never by REFERENCE syntax. PATH mutation adds host dependency and filesystem effect; URI mutation adds network dependency and network effect; OUTPUT or another authorized non-filesystem, non-network, non-memory, non-STATE addressable target adds state effect and its required dependency. MEMORY and STATE targets are prohibited; use core.memory_write or core.state_update. Resolve the selected change profile within those classes.
preconditions: target is not MEMORY or STATE; those mutations use core.memory_write or core.state_update
target exists
expected_before matches when supplied
postconditions: only declared selection/properties change

core.copy.meaning: Establish a destination containing an exact copy of a source.

determinism.source: The destination content equals the exact source pre-state, the source remains unchanged, and overwrite behavior is fixed.

core.copy.invocation_resolution: Classify a REFERENCE source by the address class of its resolved target, never by REFERENCE syntax. Resolve source observation dependencies and destination mutation effects independently under the selected copy profile: any URI side adds a network dependency and network effect for the primary copy; any PATH side adds host dependency; a PATH destination adds filesystem effect; observing a PATH, MEMORY, STATE, OUTPUT, or other host-bound source adds its required dependency but no source-side effect.
preconditions: source exists
destination absent unless overwrite is TRUE
postconditions: destination content equals source pre-state
source remains unchanged

core.move.meaning: Relocate a target without changing declared content.

determinism.source: The destination equals the exact source pre-state, the original address is absent, overwrite behavior is fixed, and the selected move profile is fixed.

core.move.invocation_resolution: Classify a REFERENCE source by the address class of its resolved target, never by REFERENCE syntax. Resolve source and destination address classes independently; the selected move profile chooses rename or verified copy-delete strategy. A PATH side adds host dependency and PATH mutation adds filesystem effect; a URI side adds network dependency and URI content relocation adds network effect; removing OUTPUT or another authorized non-filesystem, non-network, non-memory, non-STATE addressable source adds state effect and its required dependency. MEMORY and STATE sources are prohibited; use core.memory_write or core.state_update.
preconditions: source is not MEMORY or STATE; those mutations use core.memory_write or core.state_update
source exists
resolved source and destination addresses are distinct
destination absent unless overwrite is TRUE
postconditions: destination content equals source pre-state
source no longer exists at original address

core.rename.meaning: Change a target identifier/path name without changing content.

determinism.source: The exact legal new name, overwrite flag, target snapshot, and selected rename profile preserve content and all non-name properties.

core.rename.invocation_resolution: Classify a REFERENCE target by the address class of its resolved target, never by REFERENCE syntax. Require new_name to differ from the current target name. PATH mutation adds host dependency and filesystem effect; URI mutation adds network dependency and network effect; OUTPUT or another authorized non-filesystem, non-network, non-memory, non-STATE addressable target adds state effect and its required dependency. MEMORY and STATE targets are prohibited; use core.memory_write or core.state_update.

constraints: not empty
contains no path separator

preconditions: target is not MEMORY or STATE; those mutations use core.memory_write or core.state_update
target exists
new_name is legal
new_name differs from the current target name
renamed destination is absent unless overwrite is TRUE
postconditions: target is addressable by new_name and not by its prior name
content and non-name properties are preserved

core.delete.meaning: Ensure an authorized target is absent.

determinism.source: The exact target snapshot, recursive flag, require-exists flag, authorization, and selected delete profile fix the required absence postcondition.

core.delete.invocation_resolution: Classify a REFERENCE target by the address class of its resolved target, never by REFERENCE syntax. PATH mutation adds host dependency and filesystem effect; URI mutation adds network dependency and network effect; OUTPUT or another authorized non-filesystem, non-network, non-memory, non-STATE addressable target adds state effect and its required dependency. MEMORY and STATE targets are prohibited; use core.memory_write or core.state_update. No out-of-scope effect is permitted.
preconditions: target is not MEMORY or STATE; those mutations use core.memory_write or core.state_update
target exists unless require_exists is FALSE
recursive deletion is explicitly authorized when needed
postconditions: target is absent
no out-of-scope target changed

core.generate.meaning: Produce a new artifact from declared input and constraints.

determinism.source: The selected generative capability may vary output only within the declared specification, format, variation bounds, and verification requirements.

core.generate.invocation_resolution: Resolve model from the generation profile. Classify any REFERENCE target by the address class of its resolved target, never by REFERENCE syntax. PATH mutation adds host dependency and filesystem effect; URI mutation adds network dependency and network effect; OUTPUT or another authorized non-filesystem, non-network, non-memory, non-STATE addressable target adds state effect and its required dependency. MEMORY and STATE targets are prohibited; use core.memory_write or core.state_update.
preconditions: target is not MEMORY or STATE; those mutations use core.memory_write or core.state_update
required generation capability exists
postconditions: artifact satisfies specification and declared verification
result.operation.value equals the produced material artifact

core.convert.meaning: Produce an artifact in a declared target type or format.

determinism.source: The selected implementation version and exact conversion profile, target format, preserve list, source snapshot, and destination fix the required result.

core.convert.invocation_resolution: Resolve source and destination address classes and the exact conversion profile; an omitted destination binds only the declared result or OUTPUT state.
preconditions: source format/type is known
postconditions: output has target_format and preserved properties
result.operation.value equals the converted material value

core.execute.meaning: Run an exact command, program, task, phase, sequence, action, or test.

determinism.source: Derived from the exact invoked command, program, or referenced execution graph and the immutable profile required by axis_contract.implementation_profile: non-graph mode copies the execution profile's final category; graph mode copies the graph's final category.

core.execute.invocation_resolution: A PATH, URI, or STRING executable target and its exact arguments, working directory, and environment select exactly one immutable execution profile under axis_contract.implementation_profile. Every such non-graph invocation has the process effect because it runs the executable; union process with any other dependencies and effects selected by the profile within this row's maxima. A referenced TASK, PHASE, SEQUENCE, ACTION, or TEST has no mandatory local process effect and resolves the final determinism category and normalized transitive dependency and effect unions of its reachable graph under axis_contract.implementation_profile.graph_resolution.
preconditions: target is executable and authorized
a non-graph executable target resolves to exactly one complete immutable execution profile
resolved profile dependencies and effects are within this contract and declared scope
postconditions: result.command.mode is non_graph for PATH, URI, or STRING executable targets and graph for REFERENCE[TASK|PHASE|SEQUENCE|ACTION|TEST] targets

a non_graph failure to start records started FALSE and completed FALSE without exit_code, stdout, or stderr; after start, started is TRUE and stdout and stderr are present, and exit_code is present exactly when completed is TRUE
a completed non_graph command with a nonzero exit_code has producer status.succeeded unless another producer-contract failure occurred
graph mode never synthesizes started, completed, exit_code, stdout, or stderr and records value exactly when the completed graph exposes one material primary result
completion, failure phase, effects, and OUTPUT binding are recorded through the closed result.command contract
core.execute.error_resolution: For a graph target, union the local errors, including error.reference.cycle for a prohibited graph cycle, with every applicable error of every reachable operation; for a non-graph target, use the local errors.

core.install.meaning: Add declared software or resources to an external environment.

determinism.source: The exact package or resource identity, version, source, scope, dependency snapshot, and selected package profile fix the required installed state.

core.install.invocation_resolution: Resolve network only for a remote source or package profile; resolve filesystem, process, and package effects from the selected installation transaction.
preconditions: package identity and source are unambiguous
postconditions: declared package/resource is installed at requested version

determinism.source: The exact installed-target snapshot, purge-data flag, and selected package profile fix the required removed state.

core.uninstall.invocation_resolution: Resolve host and optional network from the selected package profile, including its remote-management variant, and resolve filesystem, process, and package effects from that profile's removal transaction. purge_data FALSE preserves declared associated data; purge_data TRUE removes all declared associated data in authorized scope.
preconditions: target installation exists
postconditions: target installation is absent
when purge_data is FALSE, declared associated data is preserved
when purge_data is TRUE, declared associated data is absent

core.start.meaning: Put a process or service into running state.

determinism.source: The exact stable target, arguments, environment, timeout, readiness rule, dependency snapshot, and selected start profile fix the result.

core.start.invocation_resolution: Resolve process for a native process or service and state for a referenced execution target; remote-control mode of the selected start profile adds network dependency.
preconditions: target is startable
postconditions: target reaches running/ready state or fails explicitly

core.stop.meaning: Terminate the selected path, process, or service.

determinism.source: The exact stable target, force flag, timeout, dependency snapshot, and selected stop profile fix the result.

core.stop.invocation_resolution: Resolve process for a path, process, or service and state for an internal execution-unit reference; remote-control mode of the selected stop profile adds network dependency. For an internal execution-unit target, select the active invocation aggregate, not an immutable completed child attempt; its current allowed_next must include status.stopped or error.execution.order results. An implicit handler-context target is the originating active aggregate.
preconditions: target is running or active
An internal target must allow status.stopped in its current registered allowed_next set.
postconditions: target is stopped
force used only when TRUE

core.send.meaning: Transmit declared content to an external recipient or endpoint.

determinism.source: The exact content, recipient, subject, format, dependency snapshot, selected transport profile, and implementation version fix dispatch behavior; delivery truth is a separate result contract.

core.send.invocation_resolution: Resolve host and optional network from the recipient or endpoint and resolve the message effect from the selected transport profile.
preconditions: recipient and content are authorized
postconditions: delivery result and recipient are recorded

determinism.source: Derived from the exact selected destination and publication profile together with visibility and replacement policy: after those values are fixed, the invocation copies the publication profile's final category.

core.publish.invocation_resolution: Resolve content-source and destination address classes under the single immutable publication profile: a PATH destination adds host dependency and filesystem effect; a URI or remote destination adds network dependency and network effect; source observation adds only its required host or network dependency.
preconditions: content and visibility are authorized
destination is absent unless replace is TRUE
postconditions: only declared content is available at destination with exact visibility

core.upload.meaning: Transfer declared content to an external destination.

determinism.source: The exact source snapshot, checksum, destination, overwrite flag, selected transfer profile, and implementation version fix the transfer contract.

core.upload.invocation_resolution: Resolve source observation dependencies and destination mutation effects independently under the selected transfer profile: a PATH source adds host dependency but no filesystem effect; a URI destination adds network dependency and network effect for the primary upload; a PATH destination adds host dependency and filesystem effect.
preconditions: source exists
destination is absent unless overwrite is TRUE
checksum matches when supplied
postconditions: destination bytes equal source bytes

core.download.meaning: Transfer declared content from an external source into scope.

determinism.source: Derived from source pinning or mutability, the optional checksum, source profile, destination snapshot, and selected transfer profile: the invocation is deterministic exactly when the source profile fixes one immutable source identity and content snapshot and both source and transfer profiles are deterministic; otherwise it is nondeterministic.

core.download.invocation_resolution: Resolve the source profile, transfer profile, and destination PATH independently: a remote source adds network dependency and network effect for the primary download; a local source adds host dependency but no network effect; the destination PATH adds host dependency and filesystem effect.
preconditions: source is accessible
destination is in scope
destination is absent unless overwrite is TRUE
postconditions: destination bytes equal received source
checksum matches when supplied
result.transfer.value equals the received material content

core.memory_write.meaning: Create or update explicitly authorized persistent memory data.

determinism.source: The exact MEMORY snapshot, declared value, merge flag, storage profile, and implementation version fix the post-state.

core.memory_write.invocation_resolution: Resolve the authorized MEMORY storage profile. When merge is FALSE, replace the stored value exactly. When merge is TRUE, require the current and new values to be OBJECT, form the union of their top-level field names, use the new value for every same-name field, preserve the current value for every other field, and do not recurse into nested OBJECT values.

merge.meaning: Apply the closed shallow right-biased OBJECT merge instead of replacement.
constraints: TRUE requires the current MEMORY value and value parameter both to be OBJECT

preconditions: MEMORY mode permits write
when merge is FALSE, value matches the declared MEMORY type
when merge is TRUE, the current MEMORY value and value parameter are OBJECT and the computed merged OBJECT matches the declared MEMORY type
postconditions: when merge is FALSE, the persistent value equals the value parameter
when merge is TRUE, the persistent OBJECT contains the union of current and new top-level fields, with new same-name fields winning and no recursive merge

determinism.source: The exact STATE snapshot, declared value, atomic expected-before guard, storage profile, and implementation version fix the post-state.

core.state_update.invocation_resolution: Resolve the authorized STATE storage profile, including its transaction variant, and enforce expected_before atomically when supplied.
preconditions: STATE mode permits write
value type matches
expected_before matches when supplied
postconditions: state equals requested value

core.ask.meaning: Request one exact missing value from an available authoritative source.

determinism.source: The authoritative human responder may provide any type-valid answer permitted by the exact question and options.

core.ask.invocation_resolution: Resolve one authoritative human responder. The request channel is internal to that human capability and adds no separate host or network dependency; the request is a message effect.

options.meaning: Closed answer choices, each compatible with expected_type.
constraints: Every option is compatible with expected_type.

preconditions: authoritative responder is available
request and responder are authorized and in scope
every option is compatible with expected_type
postconditions: a non-MISSING answer is recorded and compatible with expected_type
when options is supplied, every non-MISSING answer equals one listed option
when no authorized valid answer is provided, the value remains MISSING and error.required.missing applies

core.retry.meaning: Repeat the associated action under RETRY LIMIT and WHEN.

determinism.source: The determinism category and source are inherited exactly from the wrapped ACTION contract.

core.retry.invocation_resolution: Resolve the wrapped ACTION first, then copy its exact determinism, dependency set, effect set, and applicable errors. A limit outside 0..100 produces error.value.out_of_range. Before each additional attempt, evaluate RETRY.WHEN (default TRUE) as a required BOOLEAN condition; MISSING produces error.required.missing and UNKNOWN produces error.value.unknown. A prior pre_effect attempt with effect_state none requires no additional effect-safety proof. After known effects, exact retained evidence must prove safe repetition, resumption, or reconciliation within the wrapped action's original authority, scope, and post-state; missing proof produces error.required.missing, UNKNOWN proof produces error.value.unknown, and proved-unsafe repetition produces error.operation.precondition. An indeterminate prior attempt prohibits another attempt until reconciled. Retry adds no authority and no dependency or effect class. The wrapped ACTION's RETRY block is the only attempt bound: this row authorizes that declared RETRY rather than opening a second budget, total attempts are at most 1 + that LIMIT, and a resolved limit unequal to it or a wrapped ACTION declaring no RETRY block produces error.operation.precondition. Stop after the first successful attempt. RETRY.DELAY alone supplies a nonnegative delay, default DURATION(0, unit.second); a negative delay produces error.value.out_of_range. A false RETRY.WHEN preserves the previous failure and prevents another attempt. Count exhaustion requires 1 + LIMIT actual unsuccessful attempts. The budget is shared by all handler invocations for this ACTION invocation and resets only for a separate ACTION invocation.
preconditions: The selected handler is handling an event of this same active ACTION invocation aggregate; its failed attempt is immutable evidence and the existing RETRY budget is consumed.
wrapped ACTION resolves exactly once before any retry decision
wrapped ACTION declares a RETRY block whose LIMIT equals the resolved limit
before an additional attempt after known effects, exact retained evidence proves safe repetition, resumption, or reconciliation within inherited authority, scope, and post-state
an indeterminate prior attempt is reconciled before another attempt
postconditions: attempt count never exceeds 1+limit
every attempt and its local diagnostics, phase, effects, and OUTPUT binding are evidenced in attempt-index order
aggregate failure phase and effects account for every attempt made
A successful attempt ends retrying; a false condition or safety refusal is not count exhaustion and does not turn a failed attempt into success.
core.retry.error_resolution: Before inheritance, use error.reference.unresolved when the wrapped ACTION does not resolve exactly once and error.reference.cycle when its reference graph contains a prohibited cycle. For an additional attempt, use error.required.missing for missing safety proof, error.value.unknown for UNKNOWN safety proof or condition, and error.operation.precondition for proved-unsafe repetition; a safety-blocked unmade attempt is not exhaustion. Otherwise union the local retry errors with every applicable error of the wrapped ACTION contract, including any wrapped operation or profile precondition error.

core.continue.meaning: Request continuation at the declared successor after the selected handler successfully handles its originating event.

determinism.source: The handled event and exact declared successor fix the resumed execution path.

core.continue.invocation_resolution: Resolve the originating execution unit and its exact declared successor in the currently selected handler context. Record the continuation request; recovery and advancement commit together only after the selected handler, including any successful FALLBACK, succeeds. An absent or mismatched selected-handler context produces error.operation.precondition; an invalid declared successor uses error.execution.order.
preconditions: The selected handler is handling the current event of this same active originating invocation aggregate, and an exact declared continuation path exists.
postconditions: On successful handler completion, the originating diagnostic is handled and execution resumes at the exact declared successor; a failed handler never advances.

core.cancel.meaning: Terminate because the invoking authority cancelled execution.

determinism.source: The invoking authority, exact execution-unit target, and recorded reason fix the cancellation transition.

core.cancel.invocation_resolution: Resolve only the referenced internal execution-unit state, require its registered allowed_next set to contain status.cancelled, and record the exact reason. A supplied target is an active invocation aggregate, never a completed attempt; an implicit handler-context target is the originating active aggregate. Explicit cancellation outside a handler remains permitted under the registered authority and transition checks.
preconditions: invoking authority may cancel target
target current status has status.cancelled in its registered allowed_next set
postconditions: target reaches status.cancelled
reason is evidenced

expression_fragment_contract.syntax: After STRING decoding, consume exactly one EXPRESSION from 04_GRAMMAR/10_COMPLETE_EBNF.ebnf, followed only by optional whitespace. No declarations, statements, operation invocation, or named expression-call argument is admitted.
expression_fragment_contract.lexical_profile: Use the source character, string, identifier, and token rules. The fragment is one logical expression and introduces no indentation blocks.
expression_fragment_contract.environment: REF references resolve in the enclosing document and read values under types_v0.1.0.json#/reference_context_contract. Bare names in fragments denote only declared local bindings, reserved target or item where provided, or contextual enum/qualified-identifier data. They never implicitly read a document declaration; use REF for that value read. Bindings are immutable snapshots; an unknown binding name produces error.reference.unresolved.
expression_fragment_contract.bindings: core.calculate bindings is a closed OBJECT with simple-identifier keys; keys must not collide with any visible declaration ID or its simple name, any registered reserved word, or target. The reserved target binding is the resolved TARGET value, or MISSING when TARGET is omitted.
expression_fragment_contract.predicate: core.select and core.filter STRING predicates use the same fragment syntax with exactly one additional reserved binding item, the current member value. Each member is evaluated independently; there is no implicit index or external binding object.
expression_fragment_contract.diagnostics: Malformed fragment syntax and invalid bindings produce error.operation.parameter. Valid fragments retain the normal expression diagnostics; a required final result of MISSING produces error.required.missing and UNKNOWN produces error.value.unknown.
expression_fragment_contract.evaluation: Use operators_and_functions_v0.1.0.json expression evaluation and special-value rules. Static checks cover the complete fragment; dynamic errors arise only from evaluated subexpressions.
